sources.facts: Bernard O’Kane field survey, catalog 26, pp. 150–155. The central dome chamber is surrounded by an ambulatory and lateral rooms. One barrel-vaulted iwan, two niches on each side, plain brick sides and rear, and cylindrical minarets projecting from the facade. Written facts only.
Mashhad al-Reza, p. 3509 in PDF text extraction. The iwan is on the northern elevation and 9.4 m high. The double-shelled dome is 17.4 m high.
The measured front iwan span is about 4.95 m, its depth 4.2 m, and the two surviving minaret heights are approximately 20 and 15.4 m.

The pointed bays and main iwan opened onto the outside, and the outer dome sits behind the iwan. The band above the square chamber is octagonal, then a 16-sided transition supports the outer bulbous crown. The two detached-looking minaret shafts flank the entrance range.

Elahizadeh et al. identify the building as the Timurid Shah or Imam Mosque southwest of Gawharshad, along the former Chain Bazaar. The tile inscription program is documented. Pattern geometry is independently abstracted.
